body: Using `bind()` again (like a Russian nesting doll) will cancel the `source`'s emission (not the original arguments) if unbinding is enabled (`unbind > 0`).

Because `bind()` and `unbind()` are like Russian nesting dolls. The parameters used in the signal definition are the outermost layer. 

So the initial implementation of #60143 involved appending the source object to the beginning of the receiving function's parameter list. The order in which the Russian nesting dolls are opened:

> [source] [signal parameters] [unbind] [bind arguments]

However, @reduz disagreed at the time. So the current order is...

> [signal parameters] [unbind] [source] [bind arguments]

Initially, it was also implemented in `Object`. However, if implemented in `Object`, it would be necessary to determine and undo the nested layer of `unbind()`, then `bind(source)` ~~(if considering user scripts, there are many levels of nesting, this doesn't seem sufficient to guarantee the position of the source)~~, and then wrap it back to `unbind()`. And it seems that `CONNECT_APPEND_SOURCE_OBJECT` is primarily used for connecting dialogs. That's why it is the way it is now.

The current order in this PR is...

> [signal parameters] [source] [unbind] [bind arguments]

This also seems to be the reason that prevented #60143 from being merged for a long time. 

Currently, the first order seems to be the easiest to implement.
OK, should be fixed. I've also moved the `(source)` indicator between the unbinds/binds to better indicate the final arg order:
Is this branch only for the comment? 🙃

Yep. 🙂 I guess it could be moved before the `if` if that's preferred over an empty `else` block (the explanation itself why there's no error etc. in case `source_index < 0` I think is needed/helpful).

+			On signal emission, the source object is automatically appended after the original arguments of the signal, regardless of the connected [Callable]'s unbinds which affect only the original arguments of the signal (see [method Callable.unbind], [method Callable.get_unbound_arguments_count]).
